name: Humanitarian funding gap
value: WFP Gaza cuts; Ethiopia rations at 60%
summary: WFP cut Gaza food aid for 500,000 people; its Ethiopia plan is 46% funded with rations at 60%; Sudan shelter running out
state: WFP said in October that about half a million people in Gaza would lose food assistance because of funding cuts. Its Ethiopia plan for November to April is 46% funded, a $251m gap, with cereal rations at 60% (Ethiopian Business Review). IOM and UNHCR warn that millions in Sudan risk losing emergency shelter as funding runs out. Searches on 11 Nov found no formal large-scale suspension of food or health aid in famine-risk countries.
for_you: Ration cuts tend to raise malnutrition and push people to move. OCHA's Financial Tracking Service and WFP publish official funding figures.
rubric_hit: Watch: major ration cuts announced (Gaza, Ethiopia at 60%); no pipeline break suspending aid (Alert line)

sources.title: WFP — Funding cuts force WFP to drastically reduce lifesaving assistance in Gaza
Ethiopian Business Review — WFP faces $251 million funding gap, keeps food rations at 60%
IOM — IOM and UNHCR warn millions in Sudan risk losing emergency shelter as funding runs out

why: When appeals go unfunded, food aid and health services are cut first; funding gaps lead famine and displacement by months.
drivers: Donor budgets and aid cuts, new crises competing for funds, access constraints.

rubric.alert: Pipeline breaks forcing large-scale suspension of food or health aid in famine-risk countries.
rubric.watch: Funding more than 10 percentage points behind recent years at the same point, or major ration cuts announced.
rubric.normal: UN global appeal funding in line with recent years; no major ration cuts.
